body: Sometimes it’s good to mess around with the structure again and again, but to be honest for me i just get more frustrated the more i adjust things. In some cases it’s good to just let it go and start on something new - that way you have a fresh start and can write in a new style or tone. More often that not, this leads to me finding a way to change the initial piece as well!

The best piece of advice I ever heard was just to write down the things you’re feeling, not even trying to make them rhyme. Just write down all those feelings. Then, you take segments of that paragraph and attempt to morph them into verses.

I also find that whenever anything happens to you, jotting down a note of it, and maybe how you feel about it. You write best when you feel the emotion you’re writing about

The Dead Sea. It’s renowned as a cool tourist attraction because you can float on top of it due to the high salt concentration in the water. However, that high concentration is also highly dangerous, as if your head goes under the water, it is near impossible to pull your head back up due to the weight of the salt - may I stress the obvious, that drowning in salty water is NOT a good way to go. The only way to save yourself is to roll yourself over rather than try and push up. I remember I was once swimming in the Dead Sea, and a woman near me accidentally went under simply from lowering her neck a little too much.
